Canonical games model stable inference; bootstrap games reflect early-stage uncertainty; gated games embody consensus failure. These primitives form a layered causal lattice where each state transition is governed by evidence density and confidence thresholds. Failure modes include insufficient book reports (bootstrap), low consensus (gated), and misaligned predictions (loss autopsy). The system enforces a contract through immutability of fixtures, ensuring that evolution occurs via new files rather than modifications.
